pathways.climate_pressure: Drought and climate-related disasters that reduce nearby water/fuel availability.
pathways.documented_impact: Longer collection journeys and greater unpaid care demands for rural women and girls.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Gendered allocation of domestic work, poverty and unequal access to assets/protection constrain safe alternatives.
pathways.possible_consequence: The CCDR describes heightened harassment/sexual-assault exposure and lost educational/economic opportunities; no estimated climate-attributable incidence.
alternative_explanations: Pre-existing gender inequality, poverty, protection-service availability and violence independently affect safety.
pathways.uncertainty: Conditional mechanism in 2025 CCDR synthesis, not event-level attribution, a village-specific finding or a measured rise in violence.
resilience_factors: The report recommends gender-responsive disaster planning and locally inclusive institutions; effectiveness remains unevaluated.
pathways.compact_statement: The Gabon CCDR describes how drought/disaster-related collection burdens can expose rural women and girls to protection risks through gendered work and constrained safe alternatives; this is a conditional mechanism, not an incidence estimate.

gaps: No measured climate-caused violence rate or verified insecurity-to-adaptation constraint was found. National protection and resource-tension narratives must not be assigned to specific coastal towns without evidence.
NAP-II consultation locations are planning coverage, not equal local exposure or verified implemented adaptation.

executive_assessment.text: Libreville flood-exposed built-up land and coastal risks around Port-Gentil provide named examples, not a nationwide municipal ranking.

The CCDR describes a conditional water-collection/protection mechanism for rural women and girls; the NDC's resource-tension framing is national and prospective. Local planning processes are not evaluated outcomes.
